title: Corrective and Preventive Action with Effectiveness Checks

content.overview: Corrective action addresses a detected cause; preventive action reduces recurrence or related risk. A CAPA is incomplete if it only assigns a task—there must be a way to verify later whether the action actually improved the process.

vocabulary.definition: Action intended to eliminate or control the cause of a detected problem.
Action intended to reduce the likelihood of recurrence or a related potential problem.
A later review using defined evidence to determine whether an action achieved its intended result.

sections.title: Fixing the event is not always fixing the cause
sections.body: Replacing a failed sensor restores service; investigating maintenance, calibration or environmental exposure may address why it failed.

sections.title: Actions need owners and due dates
sections.body: Specific accountable ownership prevents improvement work from remaining an untracked recommendation.

sections.title: Define the success measure before closure
sections.body: Repeat-deviation rate, audit finding, process measurement or performance observation can test whether the corrective action worked.

workedExamples: Retraining after repeated labeling errors may fail if the true cause is a confusing label workflow; the effectiveness check should measure future error rate.
Adding a preventive maintenance interval should later be checked against equipment failures and completion records.
commonMistakes: Using retraining as the default cause correction.
Closing actions before an effectiveness check.
content.practicalApplication: Write one CAPA with cause evidence, action, owner, due date, implementation record, effectiveness metric and review date.
content.summary: CAPA turns lessons from deviations into measurable process changes rather than administrative closure.
